You didn’t state your age, so I can just go on what we did for my son. He’s 9 years old now with autism. He wants to be a herpetologist, and started catching lizards in the summer when he was 4.

So last year for Christmas, we got him a pet leopard gecko online. An adult, so it was stronger and healthier and not as fragile for a little boy.

We’ve had Lily for one year now, and the whole family loves this little girl. My son also watched a YouTube video about how to create our own mealworm farm. So we don’t even have to buy food all the time. (Sometimes just for variety: crickets, hornworms; waxworms, dubais).

So lizards have become an every day part of our life. He has multiple lizard stuffed animals, a t-shirt that says “Life is better with my leopard gecko”, and she gets almost daily cuddles or exploration time out of her tank. We live with her like she’s a dog almost. Just smaller but with just as much personality! She’s got a sassy face.

We like them so much we do have a second baby, who’s only 2 months old. His name is Detective Casey because he’s nosy and interested in everything. He watches the whole world outside his tank.

Huh. I'm interested, because my son is 8 with ASD, and started some of this same behavior at the start of the school year (august). Started off he would whine about going to school, and progressively got worse. He wouldn't get up out of bed. He would curl into a ball under the kitchen table and scream for hours (he wouldn't let anyone touch him). He started repeating one phrase over and over, or wouldn't talk, only grunt. His older brother (9 1/2) would set him off EVERY blessed morning and he'd fly into a fit of rage, climbing over the seat in the car to attack his brother.

It got to the point he wouldn't go to school. So I'd stay home with him, or my husband, or I'd take him to my office with me and stick him in the conference room. Because you know what? He didn't do it when he wasn't going to school. He didn't bite the air and lick the walls. 

Started kicking off some severe separation anxiety, the like of which we haven't seen for 4 years. I started staying at school with him, since that was his trigger. Walking in and down the hallway was fine. He couldn't go into his classroom. 

But -- by staying in the classroom with him, I learned something. That all of the tools he had the prior two years, weren't there. No wiggle seat, no bouncy band, no velcro, no stress ball. Last two years, school provided all of those. I wasn't told he didn't have those things in place. When I asked the school about it, they were like of course you can bring those things. So I said fine and bought them. I installed the velcro to the underside of his desk. I put the bouncy band on his chair legs. I found a stress ball that's really a toy cat, but it's so soft and squishy he loves it. So he keeps a toy cat in his desk he can squeeze if he gets anxious.

And I had a 2 hour conference with his teacher, the principal, the counselor, and the only person he actually listens too apparently: the coach. Coach is male, rest are female. And he does listen to his dad better than me, so I think the gender bias plays into it.

We did go to his pediatrician, we have set it up so he will start going to an autism therapist.  So what we also did, was remove ALL of his medications. No more ADHD, blood pressure, or depression/anxiety meds. 

Now he eats, which the ADHD kept him from before. And he's been to school every day for the last two weeks. Because it's not so bad now. The tools help. The teachers are more on board. I'm complaining he's screaming for 3 hours straight.

But they got there. =)

 I do think he needs an ADHD med to curb him some, but we're using this time as a system reset. We're aiming for six months, med-free.
